construction: Ordinary T^M=I, departure g=x, line (no base wraps). Global pulses use H at the first tick for a splitter or I for passive transport. All later pulses are I or X according to changes in the R-start word. Its complementary path is then automatic, even on overlapping broad packets. No arm-label read or arbitrary unsigned sheet increment.
closed_map: For either first direction s=+/-1, final site equals its initial x, final rail is -s, and sheet gains 2a*x+s*d. Active split includes 1/sqrt(2) and a minus only for incoming L with s=L. Passive input follows its existing rail with no split. Complete signed integer maps for mixed sites, mixed signs and both rails are checked against literal ticks.
sharp_time: Every returning n=2a path satisfies |x_t-x0|<=min(t,2a-t). Hence its centred area is between -a² and +a²; opposite extremal paths saturate relative diameter 2a². For h=2*pi/M approaching a quadrature modulo 2*pi with relative error o(1) requires n >= (1-o(1))*sqrt(M/2) on this fixed physical stride. In pulse family starting R and ending L, freezing the two endpoints leaves a-1 of each middle step. Their inversion counts cover 0..(a-1)^2, changing area by 2. Allowed areas are exactly a²-2(a-1)^2,a²-2(a-1)^2+2,...,a². Nonempty minimal lengths are checked separately for positive, zero and negative d. A zero-area target admits zero passive duration, or an onsite H splitter if such a gate without streaming is supplied; this is different from a nonempty R-to-L routed return.
precision: Terminal rail ratio L/R=exp(-i*2d*h) on an R launch, removing the common phase including the x-dependent momentum kick. Unwrapped nearest d to M/8 gives angular error <=2*pi/M, in O(sqrt(M)) streaming time with O(1) parity overhead. Table reports positive target +1/4 for theta=2d*h in turns; the ratio has its negative. Modular phases form the order M/gcd(M,2) subgroup; exact quarter iff 8 divides M. Odd-cycle wrapping can give a better phase than the fastest unwrapped construction; the separate modular table does not identify its global angular optimum with the short unwrapped latency.
latency_scope: This lower bound concerns phase differences of two fixed equal-time returning physical histories, not arbitrary filtering, pre-existing superpositions or complex controls. Changing to predetermined real X/I steering after a split is a supplied apparatus. Arbitrary complex phase gates would supply the phase being generated. The common momentum kick has magnitude 2a|h| and must be included in a packet flight; this checker does not simulate it.
selective_instrument: Use unmodified H each stream tick. Copy the first split direction coherently into a blank bit; after subsequent ticks project only on the predicate current rail = prescribed direction times private first rail. Every successful report is shared by both complementary words. Retain all failed branches separately. Since the success word ends opposite to its first rail, bit XOR controlled by final R returns the bit to blank. For an initial R the two H products have the same sign: the number of turns is odd and the number of equal successive directions among 2a-1 transitions is even. Distinct output rails make the success effect 2^(1-2a) on that initial rail. Tests include all R-start L-end zero-displacement words through eight ticks and extended signed initial data. Accepted spinors match real pulse routing after common amplitude normalization. Native H is unchanged, but the coherent first-rail copy, relative predicate projectors, bit erasure and synchronized report/control are still required. At a of order sqrt(M) the postselection cost can be exponential, even if 2a streamed flight ticks are short. Dark phase-sensitive recombiner requires no surviving arm label. For arbitrary relative-direction masks the same count and bit erasure hold; the two H products acquire relative sign (-1)^(number of equal consecutive directions). Recombination of a localized launch at one base site requires a returning pair.
detector_scope: Final H reads a cosine and cannot resolve orientation on its own. Difference of the bright probabilities of the d-e and d+e loop settings equals sin(2dh)sin(2eh). All route tags, if present, must be coherently erased. A permanent orthogonal record of the two arms instead gives 1/2 under both H readouts. Absolute conjugation leaves all real-device records unchanged.
